haiku-low.q1: Connection returns, app comes to foreground, and every 60 seconds while online.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it. It accepts an upload only if the row's base_version equals the note's current version.
haiku-low.q4: The first phone's edit is stored as note N at v4. The losing edit is stored as a new note, "N title (conflict)", v1.
haiku-low.q5: One change: the latest full title and body, with the original base_version and change_id from the first edit.
haiku-low.q6: It stores each change_id and its result in applied_changes. A retried change returns the stored result and applies nothing.
haiku-low.q7: In sync_state as cursor, the highest seq applied. It updates in the same local transaction that applies each download page.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing from that page is applied and the cursor does not move, so the next sync requests the same entries again.
haiku-low.q9: The upload response's conflict result tells the phone. The next download replaces its note with the server's version.
haiku-low.q10: Only after the phone reads that row's result in a server response. Lost or timed-out responses leave it queued.
haiku-low.q11: The phone keeps its local text, moves the cursor on, and keeps the pending change's original base, so upload reports a conflict.
haiku-low.q12: The new text goes only into notes and the in-flight row is untouched. After accepted, a new outbox row is queued. On conflict, the text is lost (open item).

sonnet.q1: Connection returning, app coming to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while online (a trigger mid-sync is ignored).
sonnet.q2: Upload the outbox first (all batches, until empty), then download from the change log.
sonnet.q3: The server. It accepts an upload only if the change's base_version equals the note's current server version; otherwise it is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first phone's edit is accepted (note at new version, e.g. v4). The second phone's edit conflicts and is saved as a new note titled "<title> (conflict)" at v1 holding the loser's body. Both notes are in the change log, applied_changes records both results. Text is never merged.
sonnet.q5: One outbox row per note: edits collapse, overwriting title and body, keeping the original base_version and change_id. It sends one change with the full latest body (not a diff).
sonnet.q6: Each upload carries a change_id; the server's applied_changes table remembers every handled change_id with its stored result. A retry returns the stored result (accepted or conflict with note id) and applies nothing.
sonnet.q7: In the phone's sync_state table as the cursor (highest log seq applied). It is updated in the same local transaction that applies each downloaded page.
sonnet.q8: Nothing from the partial page was applied and the cursor did not move, so the next sync requests the same entries again; none are skipped or applied twice.
sonnet.q9: The upload response returns a conflict result with the conflict note id (the phone deletes its outbox row). The subsequent download brings the server's current version of the original note, replacing the phone's copy (written because its version is higher than local server_version), and the conflict note holding the loser's text also arrives.
sonnet.q10: Only after the phone reads that row's result (accepted or conflict) in an upload response. Timeouts, crashes or lost responses leave it queued and it is resent with the same change_id.
sonnet.q11: If the note has a pending outbox row, the phone does not overwrite the local text but still advances the cursor. The pending change keeps its original base, so the server reports a conflict at upload and the losing text becomes a conflict note.
sonnet.q12: The in-flight outbox row is left untouched; the new text is written to notes only. After an accepted ack, the phone creates a new outbox row with a new change_id and base_version equal to the version returned in the ack. If the in-flight change comes back as conflict, the later text is lost when the download replaces it (open item).
